URL: https://www.timesofisrael.com/israeli-security-cabinet-okays-limited-international-stabilization-force-entry-into-gaza-for-pilot/
(WebFetch extract — Times of Israel's own reporting language)

Israeli security cabinet approved limited entry of the International Stabilization Force (ISF) under a Board of Peace-led plan for Gaza (approved 26 July 2026). Some 200 troops from friendly countries (e.g. Uganda, Morocco) to deploy initially along the borders of a pilot humanitarian zone (Rafah). Israeli troops to withdraw from the pilot zone, replaced by ISF personnel; vetted Palestinians could relocate from Hamas-controlled territory.
Vote: National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir against; FM Gideon Sa'ar in favour.
Board of Peace official: "These pieces are all moving forward. It just takes a little time."
Hezbollah: report that "Netanyahu talked [Senator Lindsey] Graham out of lobbying Trump to join war on Hezbollah"; no new substantive Hezbollah escalation. A senior Israeli defence official said Hezbollah is "far from disarming"; Israel to keep its buffer zone in southern Lebanon until the Lebanese Armed Forces can dismantle Hezbollah.
